question: Given `app/dashboard/@analytics/revenue/page.tsx`, what URL path renders this component?
explanation: Named slots prefixed with `@` are organizational route branches passed as props to the parent `layout.tsx` and are completely omitted from the public URL path.

question: Suppose `app/dashboard` defines both `settings/page.tsx` (in `@children`) and `@analytics/page.tsx`, with no `settings` route or `default.tsx` inside `@analytics`. What happens when a user clicks `<Link href="/dashboard/settings">` from `/dashboard`?
options: Next.js immediately renders the nearest 404 Not Found boundary.
`@children` updates to `settings/page.tsx` while `@analytics` stays mounted with its previously active `/dashboard` view.
The browser performs a full-page reload to `/dashboard/settings`.
explanation: On soft navigation (`<Link>`), Next.js retains the previously active view of any slot that does not have an explicit route matching the destination URL.

question: Using the same file structure from the previous question (no `default.tsx` in `@analytics`), what happens when the user refreshes the browser on `/dashboard/settings`?
options: Next.js returns a 404 response because `@analytics` cannot match `/dashboard/settings` on a hard navigation and has no `default.tsx`.
Next.js redirects the user back to `/dashboard`.
explanation: On a hard navigation, there is no prior in-memory slot state. Every parallel slot must match either the requested URL or provide a `default.tsx` fallback; otherwise Next.js renders a 404.

question: What happens if `@analytics/metrics/page.tsx` exists for `/dashboard/metrics`, `@analytics/default.tsx` exists, `app/dashboard/page.tsx` exists, and a user performs a hard reload on `/dashboard/metrics` without `app/dashboard/metrics/page.tsx` or `app/dashboard/default.tsx`?
options: Next.js returns a 404 because the implicit `@children` slot has neither `metrics/page.tsx` nor `app/dashboard/default.tsx`.
Next.js renders only the `@analytics` slot and omits `children`.
explanation: The standard `children` prop is an implicit parallel slot (`@children`). If a sibling slot introduces a sub-route like `/dashboard/metrics` that `@children` does not define, `app/dashboard/default.tsx` is required for hard reloads.
